text:
Bitcoin trading remains compressed near $61,500 as the macro landscape transitions into a persistent risk-off environment. With U.S. annual inflation accelerating to 4.2% and new Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh signaling a shift away from monetary easing, futures traders have priced out near-term interest rate cuts. Concurrently, regulatory parameters continue to tighten as the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority advances licensing frameworks alongside ongoing transitional provisions under Europe's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) guidelines.

This confluence of macro headwinds and regulatory friction has flattened retail demand, driving the Crypto Fear and Greed Index deep into cautionary territory. The price action demonstrates a growing correlation between legacy debt instruments and digital assets. As higher-for-longer policy rates support the US Dollar Index, traditional capital yields diminish the appeal of speculative vehicles. Capital contraction in sovereign bond markets remains the primary transmission channel suppressing crypto asset valuations, proving that public blockchain networks remain heavily dependent on global central bank policies.
